title: Chrysler Building
blurb: William Van Alen's Art Deco skyscraper at 405 Lexington Avenue, completed 27 May 1930. A secret 185 ft stainless steel spire made it the tallest building in the world for 11 months; seven radiating terraced arches crown a shaft dressed in automobile ornament.

systems.name: Shaft and facade
systems.description: The setback tower mass in four stages, with horizontal window bands in white and dark-gray brick emphasizing the window rows.

systems.name: Crown
systems.description: The seven radiating terraced arches with stylized sunburst panels in Nirosta stainless steel, rising from the 61st floor to the 925 ft roof.

systems.name: Spire
systems.description: The secret 185 ft Nirosta stainless steel spire, assembled inside the crown and raised through the roof in 90 minutes on 23 October 1929.

systems.name: Automobile ornament
systems.description: Stainless steel ornament drawn from Chrysler automobiles: eagle gargoyles, radiator caps, hubcaps and wheel motifs, plus the three street entrance portals.

systems.name: Lobby
systems.description: The three story lobby interior with Red Moroccan marble, onyx, and the Edward Trumbull ceiling murals.

systems.name: Structure and core
systems.description: The steel frame column grids, floor plates, the central core, and the 32 elevators, revealed when the model is exploded.

systems.name: Setbacks and cornices
systems.description: Cornice bands and open terrace decks at the 16th, 23rd and 30th floor setbacks, with the roof platform and crown parapet.

systems.name: Lighting
systems.description: Floodlighting for the stainless steel crown, the spire aviation beacon, and the entrance canopy lights.
